subtitle: In the Valleys of Faith and Fire

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Sikandar standing between the Jamia Masjid and distant ruins of Martand against a brooding Kashmiri sky
panels.action: Sikandar Shah stands stern and still in royal robes, one hand resting on a mosque wall, the other facing toward the ghostly outline of shattered stone temples on the horizon, snow peaks rising beyond.

dialogue.text: In late 14th‑century Kashmir, Sultan Sikandar Shah raised mosques and schools—yet Sanskrit and Persian chronicles remember him as But‑Shikan, the breaker of temples. How did one reign carve such opposite memories?

i18n.hi: १४वीं सदी के आखिर में कश्मीर में सुल्तान सिकन्दर शाह ने मस्जिदें‑मदरसों बनवाए—पर संस्कृत और फ़ारसी इतिहास उसे ‘बुत‑शिकन’, मंदिर तोड़ने वाला याद करते हैं। एक ही राज ने इतनी उलटी यादें कैसे छोड़ीं?

panels.shot: slow push-in from high over Srinagar, descending toward the palace by the Jhelum
panels.action: A panoramic view of Srinagar’s wooden houses and river bridges leads to the Sultan’s palace, where Sikandar Shah sits on a raised throne, listening to courtiers in winter light filtering through lattice screens.

dialogue.text: Around 1389 CE, Sikandar Shah took the throne of Kashmir. The valley had already seen Shah Mir’s dynasty rise, Buddhist and Brahmin lineages fade, and rival chiefs struggle for land and temple wealth.

i18n.hi: १३८९ ई. के आस‑पास सिकन्दर शाह ने कश्मीर की गद्दी संभाली। इससे पहले ही शाह मीर की सल्तनत उठ चुकी थी, बौद्ध और ब्राह्मण वंश मुरझा रहे थे, और सरदार जमीन‑मंदिर की दौलत पर भिड़ रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, slight low-angle, Sikandar in council chamber
panels.action: Sikandar Shah leans forward on his throne, hands clasped, as qadis, scholars and officers stand in two ordered lines before him inside a wooden audience hall hung with plain draperies.

dialogue.text: Muslim rule had taken root for half a century, yet shrines, priestly estates and older elites still held land, revenue and influence. To rule firmly, Sikandar had to decide: how far would change go?

i18n.hi: आधे सदी से मुसलिम राज जड़ पकड़ चुका था, लेकिन दरगाहें, पुजारी ज़मींदारी और पुराने खानदान अब भी जमीन, लगान और असर पकड़े थे। मज़बूती से राज करने के लिए सिकन्दर को तय करना था: बदलाव कितनी दूर जाएगा?

panels.shot: wide shot of Jamia Masjid construction site in Srinagar
panels.action: Workers lift deodar beams into place, craftsmen carve simple arches, and Sikandar Shah stands overseeing the rising wooden Jamia Masjid, its courtyard opening toward the sky.

dialogue.text: Persian chroniclers and later historians note Sikandar’s building hand: the Jamia Masjid in Srinagar, institutions for qadis, support for schools and places of learning, hospitals and charitable endowments.

i18n.hi: फ़ारसी इतिहास और बाद के लेखक बताते हैं कि सिकन्दर ने क्या‑क्या बनाया: श्रीनगर की जामिया मस्जिद, क़ाज़ियों के दफ़्तर, स्कूल और इल्म के अड्डे, अस्पताल और औक़ाफ़ की नेमतें।

panels.shot: medium shot at Khanqah-e-Moula, devotional gathering
panels.action: Sikandar Shah stands respectfully at the edge of a gathering at Khanqah-e-Moula, where a Sufi figure preaches to an attentive crowd inside the wooden shrine.

dialogue.text: He patronised Khanqah‑e‑Moula and Sufi institutions. In Muslim hagiographies, Sikandar appears as a pious ruler, shaping a city of mosques, shrines and disciplined law courts.

i18n.hi: उसने खानकाह‑ए‑मौला और सूफी इदारों को भी सरपरस्ती दी। मुसलिम तज़किरों में सिकन्दर एक दीनी बादशाह दिखता है, जो मस्जिदों, मज़ारों और सख़्त अदालतों वाला शहर गढ़ रहा है।

panels.shot: tight shot on Sikandar’s face in dim council chamber, half in shadow
panels.action: Close on Sikandar Shah’s face as he studies a stack of revenue documents and petitions, one side of his features lit by lamplight, the other fading into shadow.

dialogue.text: But Jonaraja, the Sanskrit court poet who lived through Sikandar’s time, tells another side: heavy jizya on non‑Muslims, bans on Brahmin teaching, exile of those who refused to bend.

i18n.hi: पर सिकन्दर के ज़माने में जीते संस्कृत दरबारी कवि जोनराजा दूसरी तस्वीर देते हैं: गैर‑मुस्लिमों पर भारी जज़िया, ब्राह्मणों की पढ़ाई पर रोक, और न झुकने वालों को जलाई‑वतन।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of the valley with Martand temple ruins on a plateau
panels.action: On a sunny plateau above the valley, colossal, weathered pillars of Martand rise against the sky, their walls visibly broken and collapsed, as Sikandar Shah and his entourage stand at a distance surveying the ruins.

dialogue.text: Jonaraja names the shrines Sikandar’s men ruined: Martand, Vijayesvara, Cakradhara, Suresvari, Varaha, Tripuresvara. Centuries‑old stone temples, emptied and shattered in one reign.

i18n.hi: जोनराजा उन तीर्थों के नाम गिनाते हैं जिन्हें सिकन्दर के लोगों ने उजाड़ा: मार्तंड, विजयेश्वर, चक्रधार, सुरेश्वरी, वाराह, त्रिपुरेश्वर। सदियों पुराने पत्थर मंदिर, एक ही राज में खाली और चूर।

panels.shot: medium shot at a broken temple courtyard with fallen sculptures
panels.action: Within a ruined temple courtyard, toppled stone lintels and cracked pedestal platforms lie scattered; Sikandar Shah stands amid his officers, gesturing toward confiscated lands visible as cultivated fields beyond.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars debate the motives. Walter Slaje reads Jonaraja’s words as genuine religious iconoclasm. Others highlight the seizure of temple‑Brahmin wealth, crucial for shoring up Sultanate power.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान वजह पर बहस करते हैं। वाल्टर स्लाजे, जोनराजा की बात को सच्ची धार्मिक मूर्ति‑तोड़ मानते हैं। दूसरे कहते हैं, मंदिर‑ब्राह्मण दौलत पर कब्जा ही सल्तनत की ताकत की कुंजी था।

panels.shot: interior shot of revenue office, Brahmin petitioners turned away
panels.action: In a revenue office lined with scrolls, Brahmin figures in traditional dress stand at the doorway, halted by guards, while Sikandar Shah, seated inside, listens instead to a Muslim jurist pointing at a tax register.

dialogue.text: Jonaraja describes jizya: a special tax for those who would not convert, and restrictions on Hindu learning. Temple teachers lost patronage; some fled. For many, religion and livelihood were tied together.

i18n.hi: जोनराजा जज़िया का हाल लिखते हैं: जो धर्म न बदलें, उन पर खास टैक्स, और हिंदू विद्या पर पाबंदियाँ। मंदिर‑आचार्यों की सरपरस्ती गई; कई भाग निकले। बहुतों के लिए धर्म और रोज़ी एक ही गांठ थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a riverside scene with camps of displaced people leaving the valley
panels.action: Along a riverbank path, groups of families with bundles and sacred objects make their way out of the valley, while in the background a royal patrol rides past; Sikandar Shah is seen distantly on a ridge with advisors.

dialogue.text: The Baharistan‑i‑Shahi, a later Persian chronicle, adds harsher strokes: reports of forced conversions, punishments, and massacres of those who resisted. It praises these acts as piety, but also amplifies them.

i18n.hi: बहारिस्तान‑ए‑शाही, बाद की एक फ़ारसी तारीख़, तस्वीर को और कड़ा बनाती है: जबरी धर्म‑परिवर्तन, सज़ाएँ और न मानने वालों की कत्लेआम की बातें। ये इन्हें दीनी काम कहकर सराहती भी है, मगर बढ़ा‑चढ़ाकर।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sikandar in prayer niche of a mosque
panels.action: Inside a mosque’s prayer hall, Sikandar Shah kneels on a mat beneath a simple mihrab, hands raised, as muted winter light filters through wooden screens.

dialogue.text: Hagiographic traditions make him a model devout king. Historian Hakim Sameer Hamdani warns that such pious tales may exaggerate zeal, turning complex policies into simple stories of saintly iconoclasm.

i18n.hi: तज़किरों की रिवायतें उसे नमूना दीनी बादशाह बनाती हैं। इतिहासकार हाकिम समीअर हमदानी خبردار करते हैं कि ऐसे किस्से जज़्बे को बढ़ा सकते हैं, और उलझी सियासत को सीधी ‘पाक मूर्ति‑तोड़’ कहानी बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a stone Brahma sculpture with an inscription naming Sikandar
panels.action: A finely carved stone sculpture of Brahma stands in a temple interior, its inscription panel carefully shown at the base, with the name of Sikandar Shah invoked in a dedicatory line.

dialogue.text: Then another piece of evidence complicates the picture: a Brahma sculpture from around 1409 CE carries a dedication naming Sikandar. Even amid temple destruction, some Hindu art and worship still found space.

i18n.hi: फिर एक और सबूत तस्वीर को उलझा देता है: लगभग १४०९ ई. की एक ब्रह्मा मूर्ति पर सिकन्दर का नाम लिखी हुई अर्पण‑लिपि है। मंदिर तोड़फोड़ के बीच भी कुछ हिंदू कला और पूजा को जगह मिलती रही।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sikandar hearing different advisers in a tense court
panels.action: Sikandar Shah sits, brows knit, as one adviser in scholarly robes speaks fervently, while another, perhaps a revenue officer, quietly presents a ledger and a map of estate lands.

dialogue.text: Chitralekha Zutshi and others see Sikandar’s measures as both religious and political: asserting Muslim rule, weakening rival elites, redirecting wealth to mosques, offices and military obligations.

i18n.hi: चित्रलेखा ज़ुत्शी और दूसरे मानते हैं कि सिकन्दर के कदम धर्म भी थे और सियासत भी: मुसलिम राज जताना, टक्कर वाले तबकों को कमजोर करना, और दौलत को मस्जिदों, दफ़्तरों और फौजी ज़िम्मेदारियों की ओर मोड़ना।

panels.shot: wide shot of Parihaspore and Bijbehara landscapes showing temple ruins and new mosques
panels.action: Across the landscapes of Parihaspore and Bijbehara, broken stone temple platforms stand amid fields, while nearby new mosques and shrines rise in timber, their silhouettes distinct against the hills.

dialogue.text: In Parihaspore, Bijbehara, Anantnag, the pattern echoed: older shrines fell, mosques and khanqahs rose, jizya marked difference. The valley’s sacred geography itself was being redrawn.

i18n.hi: परिहासपुर, बिजबेहारा, अनन्तनाग में भी यही ढांचा दोहराया गया: पुराने तीर्थ गिरे, मस्जिदें और खानकाहें उठीं, जज़िया ने फ़र्क की लकीर खींची। घाटी का पवित्र नक्शा ही बदला जा रहा था।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Sikandar’s eyes looking out over the valley from a balcony
panels.action: Sikandar Shah stands on a palace balcony wrapped in a cloak, gazing out over the misty valley at dusk, his expression unreadable, caught between resolve and distance.

dialogue.speaker: sikandar_shah
dialogue.text: A king’s choices scar stone and memory both.

i18n.hi: बादशाह के फ़ैसले पत्थर और याद दोनों पर निशान छोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of court scene late in Sikandar’s reign, with younger nobles present
panels.action: Late in his reign, Sikandar Shah sits older on the throne; younger nobles and a prince stand nearby, as petitions from both Muslim officials and remaining Hindu subjects are presented before him.

dialogue.text: By the time Sikandar’s reign ended around 1413 CE, Kashmir’s social balance had shifted. Many Brahmins were gone or weakened; Islamic institutions were entrenched. His successors inherited a changed valley.

i18n.hi: १४१३ ई. के आस‑पास जब सिकन्दर का राज खत्म हुआ, तब तक कश्मीर का सामाजिक संतुलन बदल चुका था। कई ब्राह्मण जा चुके या कमजोर थे; इस्लामी इदारों की जड़ें गहरी थीं। उसके बादशाह बदली हुई घाटी के وارिस बने।

panels.shot: montage-wide of manuscripts: Jonaraja’s palm-leaf, Baharistan-i-Shahi, modern books
panels.action: On a wooden table lit by a single lamp lie Jonaraja’s palm‑leaf manuscript, a Persian codex of Baharistan‑i‑Shahi, and modern printed volumes, their pages open to passages on Sikandar’s reign.

dialogue.text: Jonaraja mourns ruined temples. Baharistan‑i‑Shahi celebrates conversions and punishments. Modern historians sift these voices, weighing bias, faith, wealth and power without erasing the hard facts.

i18n.hi: जोनराजा उजड़े मंदिरों पर मातम करता है। बहारिस्तान‑ए‑शाही धार्मिक बदलों और सज़ाओं का जश्न मनाती है। आज के इतिहासकार इन आवाज़ों को बीनते हैं—झुकाव, ईमान, दौलत और ताकत तौलते हुए, बिना सख़्त सच छुपाए।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye shot over Srinagar showing mosques, temples ruins, and bustling streets today
panels.action: A present-day bird’s-eye view of Srinagar shows wooden mosques and Sufi shrines, scattered ancient ruins, and dense modern neighbourhoods filling the valley floor.

dialogue.text: Today, Kashmir’s landscape still carries Sikandar’s shadow: mosques and khanqahs he fostered, temple sites he broke, communities that remember exile, survival, and the slow work of coexistence.

i18n.hi: आज भी कश्मीर का नक्शा सिकन्दर की परछाईं लिए है: वो मस्जिदें और खानकाहें जिन्हें उसने बढ़ावा दिया, वो मंदिर‑स्थल जिन्हें उसने तोड़ा, वो समुदाय जो हिजरत, बचे रहने और धीरे‑धीरे साथ जीने की याद रखते हैं।

panels.shot: slow fading close-up of Sikandar’s statue-like figure dissolving into pages of chronicles
panels.action: A statue-like image of Sikandar Shah in royal pose slowly merges into overlapping pages of Sanskrit and Persian chronicles, their scripts flowing together across the frame.

dialogue.text: To face Sikandar Shah’s reign is to hold both mosque and broken temple in view—to speak the record fully, without hatred and without hiding—and let truth itself teach what power can do.

i18n.hi: सिकन्दर शाह के राज को देखना मतलब मस्जिद और टूटा मंदिर दोनों को सामने रखना है—सारा हिसाब बिना नफ़रत और बिना छुपाए कहना है—और सच को खुद दिखाने देना है कि ताकत क्या कर सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: In the Valleys of Faith and Fire
subtitle_i18n.hi: आस्था और आग की घाटियों में
